risks: Evidence comes from one seed with a cached solver: all three branch runs and this re-run are the same sample, so 10/10 is one draw, not three.
Inventories whose AND+OR count is not 6 (outside the stated rules) get an empty space and fall back to the bare benchmark turn, which this batch never tested.

If the model keeps naming non-best rows for MAX_RETRIES=4 re-asks, the harness falls back to its last informative query; if every reply was an observed or forced row, one query is wasted. Neither happened in these traces.

The 18-query margin is thin for larger spaces: in simulation, greedy best-balanced picking needed 16 queries on this batch's largest inventory (AND=3/NOT=1), 17 at AND=2/NOT=2 and exactly 18 at AND=2/NOT=3. Batches with more NOTs could leave >1 table at the end. A two-step lookahead restriction on the allowed rows is the natural next experiment, but no trace in this batch supports it yet, so it was not added.
